claims.text: The Nb-Ta-Zr-Mo-W refractory high-entropy alloy can be fabricated by laser powder bed fusion.
The proposed post-processing route is solution annealing at 1400°C for 2 hours followed by aging at 900°C for 10 hours.
High scan speed and low hatch spacing will provide rapid solidification during LPBF.
Rapid solidification during LPBF suppresses brittle topologically close-packed phase formation.
Rapid solidification during LPBF refines the alloy grain size.
The solution and aging treatments will produce a dual-phase microstructure comprising a BCC matrix and coherent C14 or C15 Laves precipitates.
Coherent precipitates can enhance strength while retaining ductility in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coherent Laves precipitates in Nb-Ta-Zr-Mo-W will impede dislocation motion and provide precipitation hardening.
The coherent character of the Laves precipitates will avoid significant embrittlement by facilitating dislocation transmission and reducing crack-inducing stress concentrations.
Adding 0.5 at.% boron and 0.2 at.% carbon during powder synthesis will cause boron and carbon to segregate to BCC grain boundaries.
Boron and carbon segregation will strengthen grain-boundary cohesion.
Boron and carbon segregation will prevent the formation of brittle interstitial-rich phases and mitigate interstitial-induced brittleness.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength exceeding 800 MPa at 1000°C.
The processed alloy will exhibit more than 10% tensile ductility at room temperature.
Unmodified LPBF Nb-Ta-Zr-Mo-W alloys typically have near-zero room-temperature ductility.
Unmodified LPBF Nb-Ta-Zr-Mo-W alloys rapidly lose strength above 800°C because of grain-boundary sliding and TCP-phase formation.
Excessive boron or carbon segregation could form brittle grain-boundary borides or carbides and reverse the predicted ductility improvement.
Changes in atomic-size mismatch or valence-electron concentration may favor FCC or HCP structures and invalidate transfer of the hypothesis to substantially different compositions.
